1) we propose an approach for remote physiological measurement based on the idea that statistics in the regions that contain noise may be similar to those in the regions that do contain the signal of interests; and 2) we demonstrate the efficacy of our approach on two large benchmark dataset for remote physiological measurement, and achieve state-of-the-art performance.

1) attention networks can be used to learn a preliminary estimate of the signal of interest; 2) a noise estimate can be obtained from the inverse of the attention mask, which is then used to refine the signal estimate; 3) our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of signal to noise ratio, heart rate and respiratory rate estimation, and generalization to new domains.
